name: Gravity letter drop and topple

source.description: 1 inspected reference film (batch-3, 2026-11-26): a pencil-on-paper launch film drops a headline's letters in from above and later topples them out of frame.

technique: The letters of a headline fall into place one by one from above with a small bounce, and later lose their footing and topple out of frame with rotation. Gravity makes the words feel like physical objects, and the exit undoes the entrance.
purpose: Make words feel like physical objects; the exit undoes the entrance, which suits undoing a claim.
visual_behaviour: Letters fall into place one by one with a small bounce and seeded tilt; later each letter loses its footing, rotates and falls out of frame.
mechanics: Entrance: each letter falls from y = -120% of the line height to 0 (power2.in), then a 6-10% bounce (back.out), with rotation from a seeded 10-20 degrees to 0; stagger about 0.03 s; a two-line headline lands in 0.3 s (ref-2860712d4e 6.78-7.06 s, 30 fps sheet). Exit: each letter takes a seeded rotation of 30-90 degrees and falls to y = +150% (power2.in), stagger 0.02 s, about 0.33 s (8.81-9.14 s).

decomposition.timing: In 0.3 s; out 0.33 s; held about 1.7 s between.

parameters.name: bounce
parameters.description: Overshoot as a fraction of line height

use_cases: A playful headline in a launch or an explainer
failure_modes: Letters colliding at landing look messy; keep fall paths vertical

implementation.approach: Entrance: the char-cascade-drop recipe (seeded character drop) with a 6-10% back.out bounce and about 0.03 s stagger. Exit (not built): per character a seeded 30-90 degree rotation and a fall to +150% of the line height (power2.in), stagger 0.02 s, about 0.33 s; seed every rotation.

provenance.observed: A two-line headline's letters drop in from above in 0.3 s (6.78-7.06 s) and later topple out with rotation in 0.33 s (8.81-9.14 s).

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
